paper_title: On the Reproducibility of Thermal Measurements and of Related Thermal Metrics in Static and Transient Tests of Power Devices

linked_assets.kind: simulation software product page (original solver, not a model or input file)

scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 3 and Appendix A Tables A1/A2, Figures A1/A2 (PDF pages 4-6 and 26-27); Zth results in Figures 6-9
scenario.description: Section 3 simulation experiment: an IGBT module (two 11.2 mm x 11.2 mm x 0.3 mm silicon dies, one powered, on a die attach, copper, AlN ceramic, copper, solder and aluminum base plate stack) mounted on a cold plate through a 50 um thermal grease layer. The study examines how TIM quality, probe lateral displacement and probe penetration affect two-point RthJC versus the TDIM structure-function RthJC. The package stack dimensions are in Table A2, but no per-block x/y floorplan coordinates are published and the power is a single uniform die-surface source. Text states a 100 W step while the Figure 4 caption says 50 W. Insufficient for a complete 2D floorplan experiment.
scenario.architecture: Power IGBT module (silicon die on die attach, copper, AlN ceramic, copper, solder compound, aluminum base plate) on a water-cooled aluminum cold plate with a 50 um TIM layer, modelled as a layered 3D stack
scenario.workload: Power step (heating) uniformly distributed on the powered die surface, simulated as a transient in FloTHERM; Zth curves, structure functions and steady-state temperature profile (Figure 5) derived
scenario.operating_point: Stated 100 W power step in text (Figure 4 caption says 50 W); cold plate modelled with a constant heat transfer coefficient of 3000 W/m2K; TIM conductivity 0.2, 1 or 4 W/mK; resulting RthJA 0.52, 0.36 and 0.28 K/W; steady state reached at about 140 s, 50 s and 30 s respectively

original_setup.solver: FloTHERM (Mentor/Siemens) 3D transient thermal simulation, per Section 3 and reference [19] (PDF pages 4 and 28)
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper reports a one-off simulation experiment with TIM conductivity varied over 0.2, 1 and 4 W/mK, and no optimization is described.
original_setup.controller: None. The input is an open-loop power step (heating) spread uniformly over the powered die surface, with a constant cold-plate heat transfer coefficient of 3000 W/m2K. No thermal controller is described.
original_setup.benchmark: IGBT module (two 11.2 mm x 11.2 mm x 0.3 mm silicon dies, one powered; die attach, copper, AlN ceramic, copper, solder and aluminum base plate) on a water-cooled aluminum cold plate, with a 50 um grease TIM. Two-point RthJC at monitor points Ch0-Ch4 is compared against the TDIM structure-function RthJC (Section 3, Figures 3-10, Appendix A Tables A1/A2).

thermal_observable.location: Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance RthJA, measured at Ch0 (centre of the top of the powered semiconductor die, in the dissipating layer), for the 0.2 W/mK TIM case
thermal_observable.aggregation: Endpoint of the Zth(t) curve and structure function (Zth = delta T_J / P) at steady state, taken at the single junction monitor point Ch0. The 1 W/mK and 4 W/mK cases give 0.36 and 0.28 K/W.

physical_mismatches.reason: The scenario is a layered 3D stack (die, die attach, Cu/AlN/Cu laminate, solder, Al base plate, TIM, cold plate) with vertical heat spreading. Table A2 gives only stack thickness and lateral size, with no 2D in-plane block placement, so a steady 2D chip floorplan cannot represent it.
The observable is transient and structure-function based (Zth curves, Cauer/Foster networks, TDIM divergence threshold epsilon). A steady-state 2D floorplan solver does not produce these metrics.

The cooling boundary is a cold plate with a constant HTC of 3000 W/m2K and a 50 um TIM layer of varied conductivity. The simulation also uses virtual probe points Ch1-Ch4 at TIM interfaces that have no counterpart in a chip-package model.

The power is internally inconsistent in the paper: the text states a 100 W step uniformly on the die, while the Figure 4 caption states 50 W. Power in a same-scenario power row therefore cannot be assigned without ambiguity.

The paper contains no optimizer, controller or reliability component to compare against. The comparison is between measurement methodologies (two-point probe versus TDIM), not an optimization or control study.

missing_inputs: No linked asset (FloTHERM model, geometry, config or data file) is included in the packet; the assets list is empty and only commercial product pages, a datasheet and standards are cited.

No per-block x_m and y_m placement coordinates are published for the powered or unpowered die, copper, ceramic and base plate, so no complete floorplan can be built. Table A2 gives only size and thickness, and the Figure A1/A2 sketches are not dimensioned for positions.
Per-block power_rows are not published. The only power is a single uniform source on the powered die, stated as 100 W in the text and 50 W in the Figure 4 caption.
The Studio package and material assumptions are not stated anywhere in the packet.
FloTHERM mesh, solver settings, ambient temperature, cold-plate internal model and the second (unpowered) die position are not provided.
Exact figure-digitized values (Figures 5-10) with provenance and uncertainty are not recorded here. The Zth and structure-function values come from text and annotations only.
